The COVID-19 pandemic has created a critical shortage of ICU beds, creating a dilemma for treating physicians who must decide which patients to admit. To address this issue, researchers have developed a data-driven approach to assess the severity of lung damage in a large dataset of 12,000 ICU and non-ICU patient images. The results indicate that certain COVID-19-related image features significantly correlate with ICU admission. The findings provide a basis for using imaging and related data for triage purposes. The underlying data is accessible at https://github.com/rodrigojg/ICU-admission-prediction.

Our study presents analytical solutions to the time-dependent Maxwell's equations, enabling explicit computation of transmission eigenfunctions and eigenvalues within a medium with a spherical gradient, along with accurate measurement of transmitted energy through an interface. Upon varying parameters, numerical simulations align closely with the analytical models. Utilizing the formulated transmission eigenfunctions and corresponding eigenvalues, we develop a novel metric, a transmitted energy function, to evaluate and differentiate the boundaries of heterogeneous materials. Through numerical demonstrations, we showcase the method's capability in distinguishing various interfaces and potentially various types of materials.

To effectively design a robot's action, gathering extensive knowledge about its surroundings is crucial.  Most exploration strategies focus primarily on identifying unvisited areas, disregarding the robot's goal to discover more about its environment.  This paper presents a new approach that combines two exploration techniques - finding areas with low entropy and following the direction of increased reward, to maximise the robot's understanding of its surroundings and facilitate goal-oriented programming.  By leveraging a pre-trained visual model to detect unvisited regions and employing reinforcement learning in a two-stage process, our method not only maximises the reward but also preserves the distinct characteristics of various environments.  Experimental results from multiple tests demonstrate the efficacy of our approach in facilitating the robot's understanding of its surroundings.

The global simplicial abelian group form of a simplicial group serves as its universal principal bundle, with the quotient by its set of global sections effectively acting as the Moore polygonization process for such groups, specifically in the context of the Simplex group S acting on any simplicial set X, similar to how an ordinary group G acts on its form G^H.

To set an upper limit on the quantity of distinct subgroups within a group, particularly for cyclic and normal transfer target subgroups, a formula has been established. This formula is expressed in terms of the order and order of divisors of the group order. To demonstrate the effectiveness of this formula, it sets a definitive upper limit on the quantity of subgroups for certain types of groups, including p-groups, Sylow p-subgroups, and nilpotent groups. Moreover, it sets a definitive upper limit on the quantity of subgroups given the order of a group. Research indicates that the formula accurately reflects an increasing trend in the quantity of subgroups as the group order increases. This finding holds true for p-groups, where it sets a definitive upper limit on the quantity of subgroups, and for p^2-q-order groups, where research has shown that the formula accurately reflects an increasing trend in the quantity of subgroups as the group order increases. These results have positive implications for understanding these groups structurally.

This research revisits the Absil-Sin-Strathman (ABS) formula, a pioneering method for calculating strain energy in deformed hexagons with six equal sides and explores how its results compare to the Neo-Hookean model under various deformations. The study investigates the effects of changing angles and side lengths on this unique hexagonal geometry, utilizing simulations in the Neo-Hookean and Mooney-Rivlin finite element models. The findings demonstrate that ABS formula significantly overestimates strain energy in hexagons with obtuse deformation angles and extremely small or large deformation angles. Additionally, the ABS formula fails to account for the influence of varying side lengths on strain energy in significantly deformed hexagons. The research also compares the ABS formula to the Neo-Hookean and other material models under various compressive and expansive deformations, illustrating its inaccuracies in calculating strain energy. These discrepancies highlight the need for an accurate representation of boundary conditions and geometry when applying the ABS formula to strain energy calculations.

The Visual Relationship Detection task in computer vision is complicated by challenging false positives, which are error-prone. This study investigates the underlying causes of these mistakes and demonstrates their infeasibility. A large number of these errors are discovered to be associated with spatial relationships, which are often misinterpreted. Experimental findings indicate that addressing this issue significantly decreases the error rate. Moreover, we introduce a dataset consisting of 142 objects in 7 categories that are commonly mistaken, which serves as an excellent benchmark for future research. This dataset is accompanied by corresponding COCO-annotations.

The connection expense of measuring a quantum system in a specific basis is currently unknown, with current estimates ranging from the system's entropy to its two-part entropy when combined with the measuring device. A new lower limit on the connection expense has been established for special cases, including strong measurement and the 'weak measurement'. In particular, it has been shown that the connection expense in performing many repetitions of a specific weak measurement on a state is proportional to the distinction between two states resulting from each measurement. This proportionality constant can be determined by a single parameter related to the measurement's interaction with the system. As the measurement becomes even more gentle, the connection expense decreases and becomes an infinitesimal fraction of the state's entropy.

Analysing large social networks is crucial for understanding behaviour in crowds and the behaviour of individuals. The objective of this research is to develop an effective method for identifying key social relationships within a network. These relationships serve as the foundation for building a comprehensive social interaction map. The proposed approach relies on identifying relevant groupings in the network, which are characterized by close physical proximity and shared characteristics. The technique employs a novel framework, referred to as a complete network, that facilitates a scalable and computationally efficient analysis of a substantial dataset. Using this framework, we developed a straightforward yet powerful algorithm for detecting significant social connections. The approach has been tested on a dataset of over 2,500 individuals, demonstrating its capability to identify essential relationships and build a comprehensive social interaction map within a crowded environment. The generated social interaction map provides a detailed representation of key social relationships and their characteristics.

Recent advances in deep learning have led to significant breakthroughs in
recognition and detection methods, primarily based on fully connected or
convolutional neural networks. However, these architectures struggle to
capture complex relationships between spatial areas, which limits their
recognition abilities. Our proposed Active Graph Message Transfer Network
(AGMTN) overcomes this limitation by explicitly modeling the connections
between spatial regions. By dividing the image into multiple parts, AGMTN
generates a graph where node features are produced using multi-scale fully
connected detection networks and region shapes are automatically determined.
An AGMTN then propagates messages between nodes in a forward-backward
manner, with the final image representation combining the original parts and
the updated features. Our method is applied to the R-CNN, C4, C3, and HoG
baselines for part-based recognition, achieving notable recognition gains on
the CIFAR10, CIFAR100, and ImageNet datasets. By comparing with other graph
neural network-based recognition methods, the AGMTN outperforms them by
significantly outscoring HoG+C4 on the 20MIL dataset and matching RNCNNAI+C4
in the performance of the 85MIL dataset.

This paper explores the design of digital constant multiplication units, focusing on an efficient method for multiplying by numbers like 0xA and 0xB. By utilizing shift, add, and save operations in place of traditional addition, the proposed algorithm significantly reduces the required hardware. A universal method is also proposed to create efficient multipliers for any 32-bit number, ultimately leading to a new structure for partial products that allows for faster processing and simpler circuitry.

Quantum machine learning is emerging technology that aims to utilize the principles of quantum physics to create more efficient learning models, particularly for tasks involving massive datasets, and has garnered considerable attention in recent years. Among the most studied approaches in quantum machine learning are quantum neural networks, which draw inspiration from the functionality of the human brain. This review provides an overview of quantum machine learning by first explaining the fundamental principles of quantum physics required to comprehend quantum neural networks, and then examining the concept along with its practical applications and associated challenges.

Radiation reaction from electromagnetic fields causes particles to lose energy, an effect that can be utilized to increase the energy of a circular beam. A Radio Frequency Booster, using this principle, enhances the beam's energy by a factor of $1+\Delta E/E_0$. Research into RF Boosters as an option for increasing the energy of existing facilities led to exploration of various technologies at work function reduced cathodes, optical cavities, and advanced particle acceleration methods. This research resulted in a successful demonstration, capable of a $100\times$ energy multiplier, which serves as a basis for future developments. These include implementing new RF Booster technologies on facilities of different energy scales, ranging from low-energy tables-top systems to high-energy colliders, which could potentially provide up to four orders of magnitude increase in energy range.

The unique capabilities of a high-energy linear muon beamline have the potential to significantly advance our understanding of particle physics through its ability to produce clear and detailed data in head-on collision experiments. Recent advancements in a muon beam have made the concept of a future muon collider increasingly feasible. This review focuses on specific challenges and potential solutions in key areas of a muon collider, including the creation of a muon beam, a technical comparison of target concepts, and the development of a reliable muon storage area and accelerator.

The properties of dispersion relations in a relativistic fluid, particularly its stability with respect to viscosity and thermal conductivity, are being investigated through mathematical modeling. By applying standard methods to a previously established set of hydrodynamic equations, a non-standard approach based on the Munoz-Alonso method yields an exact solution for any order of derivative in the relativistic Navier-Stokes and Fourier equations. This allows for an explicit calculation of dispersion relations and verification of stability. Similar calculations for other types of hydrodynamic equations reveal the presence of specific stable modes associated with sound waves, diffusion, and particle number conservation.

Our research investigates the potential for detecting low-mass primordial black holes (PBHs) with masses ranging from $10^{14}$ to $10^{17}$ grams through their impact on polarized photons and electrons near the Earth. These PBHs would emit a steady stream of gamma rays as they evaporate, which could be obstructed by the Earth's magnetic field, leading to a background of charged particles that evaporating PBHs could be detected in gamma-ray experiments observing the sky away from the Earth. We discovered that a new window of low-energy gamma rays, detectable by the upcoming CTA, may be opened by the charged particles of the PBHs, which could potentially be mistaken for signals from magnetars.

Recent years have seen a surge in interest in integrating cryptography into processor architectures.  While public-key homomorphic encryption (PHE) offers the distinct advantage of securing computation with secret data held by an untrusted server, it has a significant drawback in terms of performance.  Specifically, operations involving encryption and decryption operations (opcodes) result in a rapid decline in performance.  To address this issue, we propose the Virtual Protected Framework (VPF), a novel processor architecture framework that leverages the Totally Ordered HE (TOHE) encryption scheme to support computation on PHE data.  By restructuring data into an array and encrypting it in parallel, VPF minimizes the total number of opcodes required and thus mitigates the performance bottleneck.  As a demonstration of its efficacy, we implemented the VPF framework in a five-stage pipeline processor over the TFHE scheme, achieving an approximate 100x improvement in performance compared to current HE-based processors.

We have developed a polynomial-time approximation scheme (PTAS) for solving specific types of combinatorial optimization problems on unweighted hypergraphs with limited edges per vertex in their interaction matrix. The approach involves adapting a previously proposed heuristic framework for similar problems on sparse graphs, specifically those editable in $o(\log n)/\log \log n$ degrees. By carefully analyzing the effects of edge density and applying structural results from related work, we successfully extend the applicability of the PTAS to instances with polylogarithmic edges. The final approach combines these insights into a simplified analysis and an efficient PTAS running time, outperforming earlier solutions.

We focus on unsupervised and few-shot learning tasks for our study, with a primary interest in few-shot text classification and established on the SNLI dataset. To achieve this, we compare the performance of various transformer models, including their self-attention and local attention alternatives. Notably, we observe that these models' pretraining significantly contributes to their success in few-shot settings, with their pre-trained vector space proving effective for direct application. Building on this insight, we also introduce a novel few-shot text classification approach, where we utilize contrastive learning to align data from our pre-trained model and the dataset, and fine-tune a small multi-layer perceptron classifier. We extend this method to accommodate both few-shot learning and standard supervised classification tasks, achieving impressive results on SNLI, with our few-shot learning approach attaining a remarkable 82% accuracy using only 100 labeled examples.

Recently, techniques inspired by quantum physics have gained significant attention in the field of computer vision, where models, termed quantum neural networks (QNNs), have been applied to various computer vision tasks. Notably, weakly-guided semantic segmentation has emerged as a promising application, although it remains underexplored compared to other uses. This work presents an innovative approach to weakly-guided semantic segmentation using a custom-designed hyperspectral quantum neural network (HQNN). The proposed model consists of a classical neural network (CNN) that extracts features from image data, which are then used to configure a quantum neural block (QNNB) consisting of two QNN layers to refine these features. The proposed weakly-guided semantic segmentation framework using HQNN (WS-SHQNN) demonstrates improved performance over traditional methods using less abundant color features for road and pedestrian classification in urban landscapes. The proposed system achieved 66% and 68.5% performance for these tasks using a visible light image and hyperspectral image, respectively, showcasing its effectiveness in augmenting limited RGB data with additional spectral information. The proposed WS-SHQNN framework is open-source available on the GitHub repository.

Observations of young planets from the ALMA telescope have revealed them surrounded by material rotating at slower rates than required to ingest the observed amount of gas. Our simulations using the RAMSES code have demonstrated that, in certain conditions, a planet's migration through a protoplanetary disk can cause it to spin rapidly and collect significant amounts of gas on its surface, despite gas rotating at slower rates. This phenomenon may occur during a planet's interaction with the disk material, causing its orbit to shift and allowing it to ingest gas, potentially explaining observed young planet masses and sizes.

We analyze a new problem in theoretical computer science, where we seek to create functions that map binary inputs to single-bit outputs by manipulating individual bits. The functions we consider are built from basic operations including bitwise AND, OR, and NOT, as well as XOR and STXOR. The critical aspect is that these operations can be executed in constant time within a specific model of computation, and our goal is to understand which more complex mappings can be achieved with these building blocks. The key findings are as follows:

First, it's proven that any function taking n boolean inputs and producing m bits of output, where the size of the mapping is k, can be realized using O(k) basic operations. The large OR, AND, and STXOR components are essential, and even with limited access to these, it's possible to solve 2-SAT efficiently, and with zero access to these components, it's still possible to solve certain problems, like 3-SAT and matching in specific graphs, at a significant time cost.

Second, any function taking n boolean inputs and producing a single bit of output, where the size of the mapping is k, can be realized using basic operations including a constant number of large OR, AND, and NOT gates, and their use shows a more efficient algorithm for at least one 3-SAT instance, showing a time complexity of O(n log^2.615555555555555555

A popular way to suggest the next item in a user's current session is based on their observed behavior pattern in that session. However, notable changes often occur within a user's session. Existing approaches, which rely on deep learning, may struggle to accurately predict users' shifting interests due to their susceptibility to overfitting and the loss of essential session information. In response to these challenges, this paper proposes an advanced neural network architecture named Self-Guided Graph. It incorporates graph-based techniques to effectively manage session-based suggestion. Notably, the SG图 model's innovative use of user-side co-training enables it to handle session representation updates within a user's session independently, without the need for manual intervention. Furthermore, the SG图 model's unique design enables it to effectively address the issues of single-user sessions and users exploring beyond their session. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of the SG图 model over recent leading session-based suggestion methods.

This research focuses on LCD and invertible codes utilizing group algebras as a framework.
We identify the ideal criteria for a group algebra to accommodate LCD and invertible codes.
The concepts of group LCD codes and group invertible codes are introduced and examined.
It is demonstrated that every group invertible code constitutes a specific subset of group LCD codes.
Additionally, we developed methods to transform group LCD codes and group invertible codes into one another.

We establish an invariant differential structure on a complex of graphs, enabling the definition of graphically divergent Feynman integrals as well-defined functions on this complex. This set of functions forms a differential field, whose relationship to the classical Feynman parameter representation we thoroughly examine. Additionally, our work highlights a previously unidentified non-algebraic differential constraint inherent to these functions, reflecting a non-algebraic invariant.

A question arises in visual neuroscience regarding how an object's attributes, which are both relevant and not relevant to its category, influence processing. For instance, does a cat's 'moving' attribute have the same impact on category identification as its 'fur' attribute? We've used an object classifier trained with an artificial neural network to investigate this, discovering that object attributes influence processing regardless of their category-relevance. A cat's movement has a comparable effect on category detection to its fur, regardless of how much they differ from other cat attributes. This is contrary to assumptions in vision science that suggest irrelevant attributes are processed last. We've found that attributes are processed in a consistent order, with each receiving equal attention, regardless of their category-relevance. This is the first time such a result has been reported, and we've used the model to test hypotheses about neural processing in the ventral temporal cortex of humans. Our results indicate that the model's processing order matches the pattern of neural responses when people view objects, suggesting that categories and attributes are processed in parallel.

Topologically protected edge states in one-dimensional systems are stable against disturbances. A new phenomenon has been discovered where protecting these edge states becomes fragile under correlated disturbances. This was first observed in 2020 in systems with special properties called non-Hermitian systems. Our research provides a comprehensive framework for understanding and creating this fragile protection in simplified models with three interacting particles. Our framework reveals that protecting edge states in these models can be controlled by the level of particle interdependence. This has led to the first experimental verification of fragile topological states in an advanced photon system, and the observation of their specific properties.

Researchers have long been drawn to Golay complementary sets (GCS) due to their notable zero autocorrelation property and various applications in areas such as RF pulse design, digital signal processing, and direct sequence code division multiple access. Although research has focused on creating new GCS from existing ones through techniques like creational methods, no comprehensive summary has been provided until now. This paper outlines four creative techniques for generating GCS from smaller sets and directly, offering formulae for these methods and stating the conditions under which they yield new sets. A comparison of these techniques reveals their respective strengths, lengths produced, and relationships to existing sets, ultimately allowing for a unified framework where all known G creational methods can be categorized under one of four categories.

In the reconstruction of topologically distinct decay modes of the Higgs boson, specifically its interactions with two leptons and two neutrinos, using the ATLAS detector at the LHC, insights are gained. The analysis utilizes an invariant mass range of 125 GeV for the four-lepton system, with additional constraints on the diphoton system and lepton pair transverse momenta, with values exceeding 25 GeV. The study covers a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV, corresponding to 139 nb^-1 of integrated luminosity, and compares simulated on- and off-shell Higgs production events against four-lepton events in the same mass range. The observed data reveal no significant deviation from the predicted standard model off-shell production events, yet a discrepancy is observed, at approximately 2.5 standard deviations, in the on-shell four-lepton events. This observation is quantified by the signal strength mu, expressed as 0.71, with a 95% confidence interval of [0.00, 0.33], when compared to the expected standard model value of 1.0. Additionally, constraints on the Higgs boson width are imposed, finding it to be less than 1.1 MeV, while also estimating an upper limit of 1.2 MeV on the off-diagonal vector boson coupling involving electrons and muons.

Change detection in remote sensing is an essential research area that focuses  
on finding areas where land cover has changed.  Currently, change detection  
methods rely on supervised approaches that are limited to specific types of change  
and require a large amount of labeled data, which is both costly and time-consuming  
to obtain.  To overcome these challenges, we develop an unsupervised change  
detection method based on a novel feature combination deep convolutional  
autoencoder (FCDCAE) that merges two images at a pixel level.  The  
architecture of the network allows it to combine features from both images  
before decoding, which helps it differentiate between altered and unaltered  
areas.  The proposed method is tested on three publicly available hyperspectral  
datasets, where comparison with other established techniques shows our  
unsupervised approach delivers improved performance.

Han and Ziegler demonstrated that $773,932 = H$ is the only number that cannot be expressed as the sum of a positive square and a unique supplement. However, we identify additional examples of such numbers, including 773,932, that satisfy this property. Specifically, we provide a number as the sum of multiple distinct square numbers, such as 12^2 + 59^2 + 746^2 = 773,932.

Quantum tunneling of valley degrees of freedom in group-IV materials has always been challenging to detect experimentally. A new study overcomes this challenge by using silicon in a scanning tunneling microscope with a Cr dopant as the tip. This overcomes the limitation of silicon by exploiting the strong coupling between valley and spin degrees of freedom enabled by spin-orbit interaction, which has never been exploited before in the context of silicon tunneling spectroscopy. The discovered interaction has been quantified and found to be quite substantial, on a magnitude of 100 meV, and is made possible by silicon's large valley splitting. The study demonstrates spin-transfer between valley-polarized silicon states and the Cr 3d orbital, which is mediated by a forward scattering process, and reveals a new interaction between Cr and silicon. The study also establishes spin-valley coupling in silicon with a magnitude of 2.5 meV, nearly 1000 times larger than that of GaAs, and suggests that this interaction can be enhanced by choosing a different Cr orientation, which may make valley-tunneling more detectable in future experiments.

Relying on a closed-loop control technique, soft optimization methods can achieve the balance between speed and control precision in under a second. Although they are frequently applied in the control of data-driven systems with nuanced dynamics, there is a lack of comprehensive libraries that facilitate the efficient development and testing of these techniques. Consequently, researchers have to depend on fragmented and time-consuming implementation approaches that are not easily transferable due to varying programming languages and numerical algorithms. To address this issue, we present a unified platform called LibOPT, designed to accelerate and enhance the experimentation and deployment of optimal control strategies through a rich collection of validated algorithms and their corresponding supporting libraries. By providing support for model identification and predictive control, LibOPT enables the effective resolution of real-world problems characterized by non-linear behavior and uncertain conditions. Through our case studies, we showcase the capabilities of LibOPT by conducting time-critical experiments on floating spherical objects and soft robotic graspers, thereby illustrating the importance of optimal control techniques in addressing time-sensitive tasks. As an open-source project, LibOPT can be accessed at https://github.com/LibOPTM/LibOPT.

Consider a transcendental entire function in the complex plane, whose generated singular value measure exhibits regular, self-similar distribution. We reevaluate the variant of Baker-Eggleston degree theorem by Eggleston, whose proof relied on the assumption that the horizontal sections of such a function are algebraic and uniformly structured. This uniformity assumption is also necessary for the application of our results. We establish a broader result, extending the algebraic growth section theorem by Baker-Eggleston to functions that satisfy a similar but more general condition.

In non-commutative spacetime where spatial coordinates do not interact linearly, the behavior of quantum particles changes from following particle-like patterns to more complex, intertwined patterns. This paper reevaluates the identity crisis of such quantum particles by considering all possible ways they can be arranged. It finds that particles with distinct labels behave similarly when their spatial distribution is taken into account, but overall, the unique behavior of these arrangements depends on how the particles are individually labeled.

The two-photon absorption transient-electron imaging technique utilizes a fast laser pulse to trigger non-linear absorption in a material and a subsequent weaker laser pulse to probe the resulting charge cloud formed during a photon absorption process. This technique is particularly sensitive to charge motion influenced by material properties and defects, making it an ideal tool for analyzing charge transport at a 3D-defect level in materials. In this study, we have applied this imaging method to a high-purity, synthetic diamond crystal and observed its charge transport behavior under two-photon excitation. We have found that horizontal charge movement dominates over vertical transport, with a material mobility value of approximately 670 cm^2/Vs determined from  in situ applied electric fields. We have also utilized computer simulations based on the Drude model to dedicate a charge carrier lifetime of around 250 ns. These results indicate that the two-photon excitation-induced charge transport is primarily governed by an inter-band mechanism.

Although deep learning techniques have achieved great success in resolving various
language-related problems, their application to Arabic text is still hindered by
insufficient data availability. To address these limitations, researchers have
developed multi-task frameworks that can simultaneously handle several related
tasks and enhance performance. This study presents the first such framework for
Arabic text, targeting the detection and classification of misogynistic content.
The proposed framework leverages a shared representation layer to connect a
common input to two distinct task-specific outputs. This was tested on two
corpora, one containing a predefined set of words for single-task detection and
another with manually annotated data for single-task classification.
Compared to existing approaches, the proposed framework demonstrated
significant improvements, with two specific implementations yielding best-in-class
results across three evaluation metrics.

This study aims to derive the existence and uniqueness of the solution for fractional backward stochastic differential equations (FBSDEs), taking into account a time-varying generator under both $\mathbb{F}$ and its minimum binary enlargement $\mathbb{F}^{\circ}$. The solution exists over a fractional Brownian motion orbit $\beta(t)$. The existence of the solution is demonstrated by first solving the predictable projection $\mathbb{F}$ of the augmented process $\mathbb{F}^{\circ}Y_{t}$, and then deriving $Y_{t}$.

In the field of control theory, there's a growing need for controllers that can function effectively even when the system they're trying to control experiences disturbances or changes. Traditional methods for ensuring a controller's robustness involve a two-step process: first designing the robust controller and then testing it on various perturbed versions of the system. However, this sequential approach can be inefficient and may not always yield the best results. To address this limitation, we've developed a novel policy optimization method that simultaneously ensures robust performance by designing the controller and testing it on multiple perturbed versions of the system in parallel. The robustness of our controller is grounded in a set of uncertainties derived from the mathematical properties of certain transformations. The effectiveness of our method is demonstrated through its ability to produce robust controllers for a quadratic control problem and is further validated using the cart-pole system.

This research introduces a unified method for combining cached data and distributed computing power, capable of addressing multiple optimal problems in a comprehensive and structured way. The method combines key concepts of file caching and distributed computation to develop an efficient algorithm for resolving these problems in a general framework. It integrates previously discovered optimal solutions while also providing a novel approach to caching in an information function form, which is more versatile and adaptable than traditional caching techniques. A notable application of this method is resolving the optimal file caching and linear network coding problem simultaneously, where it is shown that a specific linear caching scheme achieves optimal performance in a way that cannot be matched by separate optimal schemes for caching and distributed computation.

We've established a foundation for Scott's domain-theoretic interpretation in univalent type theory by introducing universes of well-founded trees labeled with equivalence classes of partial equivalence relations that conform to axioms derived from Scott's framework. These new units type theory constants, specifically bottom elements and projections over projections, seamlessly integrate existing constructive type theory mechanisms like pattern matching and strong induction. By demonstrating that our universe of well-founded trees is equivalent to the Scott domains formed by equivalence classes of PCF expressions, we've validated our framework's correctness through an induction-on-derivation-terms-on-the-terms-open-to-universes-on-POFMs-on-PERs-on-ECTCs-on-PERs-on-terms-open-to-universes-on-POFMs-on-PERs-on-ECTCs-on-PERs argument.

The cancellation of Eisenstein series at trivial spectral parameters can be understood as a direct consequence of the Langlands-Shimura-Shahidi functoriality principle. Specifically, it is equivalent to the mapping of automorphic representations from $P\times GL(1)$ to $GL(n)$ with distinct images of the $GL(1)$ component. This cancellation is inherently linked to the non-existence of certain automorphic representations and, in turn, relates to certain Diophantine problems. In one dimension, this is akin to finding rational points on specific algebraic varieties, such as the affine line over a parabola in the case of $n=2$. Conversely, for higher-dimensional cases, this involves searching for points on flag varieties defined by polynomials with entries from a global field $F$. For rational coefficients, these points correspond to certain automorphic representation submodules, a concept that also applies to general $F$ through applications of Eisenstein cancellation. Notably, this is connected to the problem of automorphisms of automorphic representations, a topic explored in a companion paper.

Mobile robotic arms operating near humans require safety assurance, especially when their movement range is not fully contained. Traditional control methods, which work well in confined areas, fail to handle accidental motion beyond these boundaries, potentially causing harm. To address this limitation, this research focuses on enhancing these basic controllers to handle uncontained motions by integrating configuration-aware safety mechanisms derived from the robot's occupancy map. By leveraging Control Barrier Functions, these advanced safety mechanisms adapt based on the robot's possible motions and consider its configuration when handling boundaries, thus ensuring safety even in the face of unexpected movements. A key innovation of this research is the formulation of a specific problem that guarantees asymptotic stability through the fusion of these safety mechanisms with the original controller, allowing for efficient implementation using only matrix operations. Extensive testing of the proposed method is provided through extensive testing of the robotic arm in various environments.

Text summarization via a non-extractive approach using sentence representations. The extraction method utilizes sentence positions in the source text, whereas the excerpt method selects representative sentences that capture the overall meaning of the summary. In contrast, our proposed extractive method aims to overcome this limitation by generating an excerpted summary that not only reflects the original text but also highlights its most significant aspects. To achieve this goal, we suggest using graph-based sentence selection in the source text. Specifically, our proposed algorithm involves constructing a graph where nodes represent sentences and edges signify the relationship between them. By analyzing the importance of each node, our proposed method can identify key sentences that should be included in the summary.

Researchers have been exploring the use of nonlinear quantum devices for precise control and fast switching in optical systems. In this investigation, we extend this concept to a Bose-Einstein condensate, utilizing a triple-well setup where two BECs are positioned in outer wells and a barrier barrier separates them from a third site without a BEC. By applying a laser to the barrier, we induce coupling between the two BEC's clouds and observe the development of a phase connection. When a second laser is applied directly to the BEC in the middle well, it induces a phase shift that can cause the BECs to collapse or not into the third well. In areas with a superfluid characteristic, this phase shift is observed to have a significant impact on the behavior of the BECs, which is not seen in the absence of BECs in the middle well.

Consider a complete K\"{a}hler manifold X and a projective variety X' in another projective variety X with hyperplane sections D_1 through d+1 that are distinct. If a meromorphic map f from X to X' avoids pole problems along a divisor with positive relative intersection, then it follows that if the pullbacks of these sections have maximal relative transcendence degree, the image of f covers all of X'. This result holds under two conditions: either the characteristic of the ground field is zero, or the characteristic is positive and the map f is morphism when restricted to a generic fiber of a holomorphic submersion from X to a base manifold B with relative ample image. This confirms a long-standing conjecture by Cartan and a related theorem from [Li, C. and X., F. (2019)] under the condition that X is a vector space and the map f is a meromorphic map rather than a morphism.

A signature is a unique mathematical expression involving variables in a polynomial system that uniquely determines the structure of its solution space. Solutions non-tritionally found in this framework exclude points where at least one of these expressions has a value of zero. We present an innovative algorithm to automatically identify and extract these unique descriptors for any given polynomial system. By doings so, our method enables a clear distinction between the distinct branches of the system's solution manifold. We extensively tested our algorithm using diverse polynomial systems, demonstrating its effectiveness and ease of implementation within a computer-aided system.

We conducted an in-depth analysis of low-energy direct photons produced in Cu$+$Cu collisions at a energy of 200 GeV per nucleon pair for both central and semi-central events. Our findings indicate that these photons significantly contribute to the overall photon yield observed at certain rapidities and $p_T$ ranges. When comparing our results to theoretical expectations derived from a specific hydrodynamic model that does not account for anisotropic flow, we observed a notable discrepancy, especially for semi-central events. However, an inclusion of anisotropic flow in our analysis significantly improves the agreement between theory and experiment, suggesting that anisotropic flow may be crucial in explaining the observed phenomena. Furthermore, our analysis also reveals that the effects of anisotropic flow vary significantly depending on the centrality of the collision.

The goal of the fully dynamic k-connectivity maintenance problem in graph theory is to maintain the connectivity status of all subsets of four given vertices within a network of possible changing connections. Specifically, in the case of $\ell_s$-norm for values $s \ge 1$, the connectivity of these subsets is determined by the sum of the connections between each subset's members. Historically, Khot and Samorodnitsky have established a lower bound of $\Omega(k^{1/3})$ for this problem when the graph network contains up to polynomial numbers of edges. In the case of $\ell_2$-norm, the single-edge lower bound can be easily converted into a multi-edge version. In the current case, we have developed a more complex connection in which $n = \Omega(k^{3/2})$ edges are added or removed, resulting in a new lower bound of $\Omega(k^{1/2})$ for the $\ell_2$-norm. In addition, we have created a more complex connection in which $n = \Omega(k^{2/3}\log_k p)$ edges are added or removed, thus tightening the Khot-Samorodnitsky lower bound to $\Omega(k^{1/2}\log p / \log k)$ for a specific range of p values. In the case of the Hamming-norm, we have found a more complex connection that closely matches a conjectured upper bound of $\Omega

Vector maps rendered using traditional methods often suffer from spatial aliasing, 
especially evident in line junctions where multiple paths converge. As rendering resolution increases, 
oscillatory patterns appear, degrading visual quality. While isotropic anti-aliasing techniques exist for two-dimensional images, rendering complex vector maps remains computationally expensive. In this study, we propose a novel method to eliminate spatial aliasing in line junctions by pre-calculating color probabilities for a high base rendering resolution and applying an efficient low-base rendering technique that utilizes these probabilities. Our approach enables affordable, high-quality rendering of vector maps at any desired rendering resolution, bypassing oscillatory patterns.

We introduce a new function to replace standard Gaussian functions in RBF (radial basis function) calculations. This new function has distinct characteristics that make it ideal for mathematical operations. It can take any value from 0 to infinity based on its input, which is a monotonic and smooth process. In addition, it approaches 0 as the input grows, ensuring stability in its use. It also approaches 1 as the input approaches 0, indicating its capability to handle data points closely. This new function enables the creation of new, stable, and accurate forms of quasi-interpolation operators. These new operators can accurately reproduce data with a low degree polynomial function and have the capability to precisely calculate values as the function's support increases. This is achieved while maintaining data accuracy in the process. Our approach includes numerical examples to accurately test and validate the accuracy of our new operators.

We have carried out a comprehensive search for neutron star shells across the entire gamma-ray bright galaxy using the 4th Data Catalogue from the HESS observatory. The shell system associated with each PNR was identified, with parameters determined in a standardized way. The analysis revealed 33 extra galaxy gamma-ray sources beyond those identified as PNR clusters, suggesting the presence of nearby neutral hydrogen clouds required for PNR shell formation. The discovered PNR shells account for approximately 60% of the known PNRs in the galaxy, with the remaining 40% likely consisting of nearby HD clouds yet to be discovered. The newly identified PNR shells significantly expand the distance range observed for these systems, extending to distances greater than 10 kpc from the galaxy's center. The formation of these PNR shells is estimated to occur over a timescale of around 100,000 years through interaction with nearby HD clouds. The PNR shells present a significant fraction of the known gamma-ray energy in the galaxy, accounting for around 10% of the total gamma-ray energy emitted by PNRs. The known PNR shells contribute approximately 1/3 of the diffuse gamma-ray background energy and about 10% of the gamma-ray background at the plane of the galaxy. The PNR shell emission mechanism is explained by synchrotron self-Compton radiation, with electrons being accelerated by the pulsar's wind interacting with the surrounding nebula.

The outdoor scene classification task is becoming increasingly important due to numerous real-world applications, such as identifying suitable parking spots and detecting incidents in traffic cameras. A successful completion of this task requires weather categorization. The effects of weather on image characteristics make it challenging to determine the weather condition in an image. Current approaches typically employ a data-driven, automated system rooted in deep learning technology. Experimental results reveal that traditional data augmentation techniques used in computer vision do not effectively increase the number of outdoor scenes. A new algorithm has been developed to increase the number of weather conditions in outdoor images. This study presents a new multi-class dataset, along with the proposed algorithm, and demonstrates its effectiveness in improving categorization accuracy. A new network architecture has also been designed to achieve superior performance. Experimental results reveal that this approach yields the most accurate results. The dataset and associated documentation are available at http://omarsaleh.github.io/weather-dataset/.

Our research focuses on how climate change is perceived by different groups based on their level of care for the environment and their social environments. These groups make up our concept of 'types', and we've identified four distinct groups with varying views on the severity of climate change, the level of scientific evidence supporting it, and the effectiveness of policies to address it. We've discovered through extensive surveys that people's opinions on climate change are influenced as much by the views of experts and their peers, as by their level of care for the environment. Our findings challenge the assumption that climate change perception is solely based on individual values, and they suggest that a more nuanced approach is needed to understand and effectively communicate the complexities of climate change, and the role of scientific and institutional factors in shaping policy and behavior.

This study introduces a novel approach for controlling soft multi-fingered grippers, leveraging the potential of soft materials while maintaining the efficiency of electrical resistance-based actuation and measurement. Due to the nonlinear characteristics and complex interactions between the electro-mechanical properties and external forces of these soft robots, linear control methods are insufficient. Therefore, this research develops a three-dimensional virtual model for each finger, which effectively mimics the actuator's electrical resistance changes in response to external forces, enabling a more accurate control strategy. By employing the data-driven Koopman operator, this team further enhances the model, leading to a precise simulation of end-effector motion with a high degree of prediction accuracy, even for complex multi-body systems. Moreover, this research successfully applies the virtual model to create a robust feedback control system that ensures precise movement across various external conditions, ultimately verifying the effectiveness of this approach through experimental validation.

The Organic Generalized Residual Gradient Descent (OGRGD) is an advanced algorithm that seamlessly integrates Multi-Parameter Optimization (MPO) and Multi-Objective Optimization (MOO) methodologies to drive molecular design processes. Our work extends OGRGD by introducing a general formulation that allows for the use of any organic solver and any geometric distance function. In particular, we introduce the metric-based OGRGD ($\mathbf{g}$OGRGD}), which utilizes 3D geometric distances to define an objective space. To validate the algorithm's efficacy, we conducted experiments using end-to-end molecular design systems based on $\mathbf{g}$OGRGD, featuring three- and four-objective properties. The application of $\mathbf{g}$OGRGD was demonstrated with both Euclidean and Wasserstein-3 distances in our tests.

High-redshift young radio galaxies provide significant insights into the early stages of radio activity. The goal of this research is to establish a high-z young radio galaxy at a significantly distant location. A particularly striking radio source, designated J2102+6015, was recently discovered in the FAST survey. It is situated far away in space, approximately 4.575 billion light-years away. This powerful object has a significant luminosity, radiating 10^40.5 Watts per square metre. Using comprehensive multi-wavelength analysis combining data from various space telescopes like Chandra, XMM-Newton, and the NuSTAR, combined with ground-based facilities including VLT and GTC, we have obtained a detailed picture of J2102+6015. This research reveals that the source is composed of two compact active black hole sources, both situated within a small spatial distance of each other. This research provides the highest redshift record for a young radio galaxy, expanding our understanding of these powerful cosmic objects.

A new approach to predicting the one-year survival rate of non-small cell lung cancer patients is proposed, leveraging educational neural networks that train on multiple types of data, including radiological, genetic, and demographic information. By combining a CT scanner analysis with blood test results and personal details, the proposed model offers an innovative and comprehensive framework for prognosis, outperforming existing methods in both single-modality and multi-step network comparisons.

This overview seeks to spark further investigation into descriptions of language states in reinforcement learning by examining their significant influence on the described system's overall behavior. In many cases, these state descriptions are presented as simplistic "one-size-fits-all" solutions, often hindering further research and development in the field.

A novel approach combining machine learning and astrophysics is introduced to reconstruct the cosmic energy spectrum from comprehensive spectra of high-redshift quasars. In this study, the absolute energy spectrum of 5788 quasar absorption features within the redshift range of 1.4 to 3.5 was recovered using the EXOSUMS algorithm, with an average rms scatter of 0.02 mag. Although the resulting energy spectra exhibit scatter, they display distinct features, such as molecular absorption lines, at various redshifts. To assess the accuracy of this approach, the reconstructed energy spectra were cross-checked against existing observations from multiple surveys, with an agreement within 0.015 mag. Furthermore, this method enables the recovery of absorption features outside the GALEX wavelength range by extending the spectra beyond 300 nm.

We investigate two types of Lie algebras, specifically those of difference and derivative operators, in relation to the Fock space and the Hardy space, in addition to a specific basis for the commutative Weyl algebra which allows us to establish an inverse Fourier transform. Overall, our work provides new insights and a comprehensive theory regarding $U(\frak h)$-vacant modules over these two types of Lie algebras.

Over the last two decades, analyzing public sentiment on social media platforms has become increasingly important. As a result, numerous studies have focused on developing automated systems for assessing sentiment in the Twitter environment. Over time, this area of research using Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques, along with advancements in Deep Learning, continues to grow in significance. In this study, we utilized three publicly available Twitter datasets, incorporating three distinct approaches. We examined the outcomes of these methods, comparing their accuracy. The results showed that combining traditional NLP features with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural networks performed better than other examined models.

Conversational systems that understand natural language and engage with users about specific topics are crucial across various domains. Despite existing, they often fall short when it comes to creating immersive characters with distinct personalities and extensive knowledge bases. To bridge this gap, we've developed an innovative conversational system grounded in a single, character-driven narrative with extensive openness. By leveraging a massive 1.76 trillion token corpus, we've trained a massive language model, showcasing its promise in NLP tasks such as textual simulations and generation. Our experiments reveal exceptional performance with scores as high as 0.316 on the 2019 Neural Textual Competition and 0.302 on the 2020 Korean Conversational Challenge. Ultimately, we anticipate this framework will contribute to the growth of large-scale, open conversational systems.

The detection of a random background of gravitational waves (GW) has the potential to offer insights into the collective activity of sources. Current detection efforts are focused on the background generated by merging binary black holes, but new possibilities are emerging in other frequency bands. In a new research approach, we investigate a different type of gravitational wave contribution that could be detectable by future detectors. Specifically, we examine the nonlinear effect known as the "memory effect" that results in low-frequency gravitational waves. The memory effect is produced by individual sources over extended periods of time, generating quasi-monochromatic gravitational waves. The stochastic background that forms from the superposition of these signals is characterized by distinct features, including a relatively flat amplitude spectrum at lower frequencies and a $f^2$ dependence at higher frequencies. Our analysis indicates that this effect could potentially be within the detection range of future detectors like the Einstein Telescope.

The R-parity conserving Minimal Supergravity Model with a single SUSY breaking source offers an ideal setting for generating large scale particle and energy phenomena, specifically high scale Baryon Number violation and strong scale Gravity Wave signals during Early Universe inflation, as well as potential formation of Black Holes following inflation. This model features topological defects known as global strings which decay, producing significant effects on Early Universe dynamics. Furthermore, we propose a novel and highly predictive mechanism for generating the observed amount of chirality violation in Neutrinos, a phenomenon known as Leptogenesis, which is driven by a phase shift resulting from the interaction between the SUSY breaking source and the fermions it sources during the formation of heavy Majorana Neutrinos. This lepton number violation then transforms into the observed amount of chiral matter in the Early Universe.

A revolutionary approach to semantic communication promises to reduce data transmission by interpreting the meaning behind messages. A key challenge in this field is accurately representing and extracting the semantic content of a message. From the perspective of information theory, a message conveys not just data, but also causal relationships. This study focuses on receiver-side causal relationship learning to enhance message comprehension in semantic communication. A novel neuro-symbolic framework is proposed, where neural networks symbolize logical inferences about causal relationships between system variables at the receiver end. A corresponding signaling game is designed to model the interaction between transmitter and receiver, where both parties make decisions based on their respective system variables. An empirical examination using synthetic data demonstrates the framework's effectiveness.

Working with written language poses significant challenges for various applications, such as text processing, searching within texts, text translation, and understanding text. A crucial aspect of overcoming these challenges is to have a vast vocabulary. But the size of the vocabulary alone isn't sufficient; it must also be dynamically responsive to emerging written forms. This研究报告 proposes an improved term prediction system that takes into account hidden knowledge from a language model. We experimented with this proposed system on three different languages: Turkish, Indonesian, and English. It's demonstrated that by combining a simple probabilistic generator with hidden knowledge from a language model, better prediction results can be achieved. Surprisingly, the outcomes indicate that the effectiveness of our framework largely depends on the quality of the hidden knowledge and can provide significant speed-ups, especially during real-time interactions.

Session-based suggestion systems have seen significant development in both online applications and theoretical research. Nevertheless, most existing models fall short in addressing user changes throughout an entire session. To bridge this gap, our proposed method, TR^2, utilizes a dual-network structure to capture user actions spanning the entire session. Specifically, TR^2 models the entire session as a sequence of time-stamped steps, where each step is represented as a vector in a latent space. TR^2 then recommends items that fit the session's current stage by predicting the vector in this space corresponding to that stage. To evaluate our session-based suggestion framework, we employed two metrics: session completion rate and session extension rate. These metrics were used to assess the effectiveness of TR^2 on real-world datasets, including Amazon, Taobao, and Google Shopping datasets. Notably, TR^2 outperformed five baseline models on all three datasets.

The movement of microscopic particles that self-generate activity within an environment that varies in activity levels has not been thoroughly examined experimentally. A study presented here investigates the behavior of a large particle that fits the criteria of a active colloid, which exists within a solution varying in activity levels. Over time, the particle moves from areas of low activity to areas of high activity, as evidenced by simulations based on a well-developed model. However, its forward and backward movement distances are unequal, resulting in a net movement toward areas of high activity levels. This net movement observed in the study agrees with the predictions made by the generalized Lowe-Capilar model.

An accurate simulation of discrete fracture flow demands high computational power, 
which can be reduced by using methods like the Mixed-H1 Finite Element method, but 
these methods struggle with complex three-dimensional geometries. To overcome this, 
a recent method based on Functional Analysis was proposed, allowing for simpler 
mesh generation and easier handling of fractures. However, implementing this method 
in three-dimensional fracture networks remains a significant challenge. This paper 
successfully addresses this issue by developing a technique for mimetic finite differences 
on conforming three-dimensional grids, which enables general network representation 
and easier meshing. This approach also facilitates easier representation of fractures 
using planar surfaces without additional mathematical constraints.

A computational approach using super-resolution algorithms and super-resolution algorithms based on centroid calculation can maintain the integrity of a complex, self-organized pattern formed by a group of drones in mid-air. By calculating the center of mass of the pattern, this method effectively removes distortions introduced during flight, allowing the pattern to be restored with high precision. Our approach leverages these algorithms in a high-level control system to eliminate errors accumulating over time and remove the effects of low-level control methods on the pattern's shape. This helps prevent collisions and不适 within the formation and restores the pattern with high accuracy.

We show through counterexamples that the proposed range for Seidel eigenvalues in a vertex-transitive graph is not accurate, then investigate the maximum energy of the Seidel spectrum in specific types of graphs, including path and cycle, and determine the conditions needed to achieve this energy in these graphs, before ultimately proving it is impossible for certain graphs to meet these conditions.

Our work centers around a mean-field optimal control problem for a partial differential equation driven by a fractional Brownian motion. The solution to this problem is a time-dependent function, whose time derivative satisfies a partial differential equation driven by a time-dependent function and a fractional Brownian motion. We use a mean-field partial differential equation to find the solution, which depends only on the time variable. The solution can be expressed in two equivalent forms: as the solution to a partial differential equation containing a bilinear term or as the solution to a partial differential equation with a non-linear dependence on the solution.

A significant challenge in V2X communication is ensuring a stable connection
between road users and infrastructure in areas with a lack of reliable infrastructure.
This research is centered on enhancing this relationship by incorporating two
distinct components: roadside units and vehicle relays. A new model has been
introduced that takes into account a mix of road users and infrastructure at the
first level, and vehicle relays along a best path trajectory at the second level.
Various levels of road components and relays are considered as stochastic processes.
We establish an optimal path for data transmission and determine the densities of
road users and relays along this path. We also introduce measures to assess the
stability of the introduced components along this path. We then conduct a thorough
analysis of the proposed model using numerical methods and provide a in-depth
discussion on key parameters influencing road users' connectivity.

Wikipedia's user-contributed model relies on diverse individuals maintaining the encyclopedia, but certain groups consistently contribute poorer quality content, specifically relying heavily on translating non-English sources. Despite being active Wikipedia contributors, these groups often produce material requiring less input, which could be mitigated by incorporating them into Wikipedia's existing quality control processes. By extracting editing behavior patterns from a large Wikipedia subset, we identified two effective high-level features that can automatically mark such contributors' additions as "incomplete" during article editing, significantly outperforming random noise additions in accuracy rates.

Deep learning models have achieved remarkable success across a wide range of tasks, but their positive impact is limited to environments where extensive labeling is feasible. Most real-world applications, however, take place in frameworks unknown to the models, making it difficult to deploy them effectively. To overcome this limitation, few-shot learning techniques have been developed to train models on a minimal number of samples, allowing them to generalize to new environments with minimal additional training. Our model architecture enables training in an unknown environment with almost no additional overhead, based on the assumption that the models can transfer knowledge from a source domain. We provide theoretical and practical evidence supporting this assumption. Additionally, we conduct experiments in image classification and semantic segmentation, demonstrating our ability to adapt models to new domains with high performance in zero-shot settings.

Researchers have seen the $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^0 K^0_L$ transition for the first time with an occurrence rate of $2.1 \times 10^{-4}$ and have also established the evidence of the $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^{*0} K^0_L$ transition. These findings were derived from a vast dataset of $pb$ collisions, totaling $3.029$ inverse femtobarns, which was analyzed using the LHCb detector.

A key geometric tool in studying topological theories like K-theory and equivariant K-theory is the notion of twisted tori, which serve as fundamental building blocks for more intricate twisted K-theory space constructions. To further develop this framework, we employ geometric T-duality – a key concept in string theory – to create a more comprehensive and structured understanding of twisted tori. Our key innovation lies in representing twisted tori through a combination of Lagrangian cycles and a specific gerbe with a gerbe connection, offering a more generative and structured perspective. Ultimately, our research provides a more detailed and structured set of twisted K-theory space axioms.

In the realm of learning, a fundamental concept is co-optimization, which involves two or more entities learning from each other's interactions with their surroundings, bypassing the need for direct examples. A study presents a novel framework for learning observation skills through the spatio-temporal patterns of hidden states in shared environments, eliminating the need for direct displays of hidden states, which are impractical in complex environments. This framework leverages the structural relationships between observed entities and hidden states, which can be independently identified as flow fields, to derive the observation skills required to track the entities' trajectories. A simple yet effective agent design was employed to test the framework on a range of two and three-dimensional shared environments, demonstrating successful learning of observation skills and, in some cases, enabling the agents to predict the locations of hidden entities after a period of non-interaction.

Recent advancements in run-length limited sequences have introduced a constrained capacity, restricting the allowable patterns. This work examines the probability distribution of these sequences under uniform distribution and derives the Mostobadi-Leung-Berrou metric. This metric enables the transformation of unbounded sequences into PAC sequences through a projection method that preserves the emission probability, facilitating the application of conventional channel coding techniques in the run-length limited domain. The solution employs dynamic programming for the exact calculation of metric values. Additionally, nearly linear-time approximations are proposed for practical applications and validated with specific sequences.

Understanding how humans interact with objects in various settings is crucial for producing more authentic human-like content and gaining insight into human behavior. Despite significant advancements, accurately tracking hand-object interactions in complex environments remains a significant challenge due to the intricate lighting and shadows. Our research introduces a new dataset called WILDHANDS, featuring video sequences of hands interacting with objects in extensive outdoor environments under changing light conditions. Accompanying WILDHANDS is a novel network called Reconstruction from Hand Interactions, or ReHaI, which splits the complex task into object tracking and reconstruction. By focusing only on the region where the hand and object interact, ReHaI can efficiently utilize computational resources while achieving high reconstruction quality. Our experiments demonstrate that our proposed dataset and method outperform existing techniques in both tracking accuracy and visual reconstruction quality.

A well-calibrated robot end-effector is crucial for robots to accurately perceive depth and for making precise movements.  However, in our study, we investigate a scenario where robots are not properly calibrated and need to be realigned.  To address this challenge, our approach involves training a model that learns to automatically correct robot depth perceptions and calculate exact end-effector positions without requiring labeled data by leveraging learned features from depth images.  Our experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of this Unmarked Robot-Depth Camera adjustment system in accurately estimating a robot end-effector's position and orientation and also in providing a foundation for further research on unmarked robot self-calibration.

A new understanding of treatment interference has been developed by Goodstein and Naidu, which defines it strictly based on a predefined cutoff for the distance between treated and control units.  Interference is considered to occur when this threshold is surpassed.  Traditional approaches to addressing this issue involve assuming a specific spatial distribution of units, such as assuming that units are evenly spread across a map.  This study critiques such an approach and instead proposes a more practical method that simply ranks units according to their distance from one another.  This revised framework allows us to identify two key areas: a zone of treatment and a zone of spillover.  Our research shows that under this new system, there is no way to know where exactly this divide lies without actually conducting an experiment to test it.  Our work builds upon existing research by Bountoukli and Toulis that looked at the effects of treatment interference under the same conditions.  Our results show that treatment and spillover effects can coexist, but that the spillover effect may be masked by the treatment effect.  Our research shows that common metrics used to evaluate treatment effects, such as the difference in means, may actually measure the difference between the treatment and spillover effects, rather than the spillover effect alone.  Our work provides a simpler way to identify when treatment effects and spillover effects are at play, and is useful for a wide range of applications including the study of interference in social networks.

Previous studies have shown that when Dark Matter annihilates inside a Neutron Star, it can produce a significant amount of neutrinos. This creates an extra source of energy that needs to be taken into account while investigating the properties of Neutron Stars. As further research has found that new types of Dark Matter interactions could exist, we have examined how multiple annihilation processes occur when the Dark Matter interacts via both a pseudoscalar and a scalar field. This detailed analysis has found that for some situations, our new results can increase the neutrino emission up to 100 times its previous limits. This increased emission could potentially be observable in current data from a NASA's Chandra X-Ray Telescope.

A novel approach for weak lensing-based shape measurement, the ShapePipe workflow, has been developed for the UNIONS/CFIS project, and it successfully re-evaluates galaxy shapes for an un lenses analysis covering approximately 1700 square degrees of the sky, containing over 200 million galaxy shapes. The existing Unions TF88 revision employs an older, now outdated, workflow for the analysis, which necessitated the creation of ShapePipe for un lensing-based cosmology research, and it has been specifically designed for un lensing work, and it has been successfully applied to un lenses data, which includes CFIS, CFHTLS, HSC, KiDS, DES, and WSRT shape catalogues, and it has contributed to the development of SHAPES, a public database of galaxy shapes, and it has confirmed the reliability of the ShapePipe workflow, which matches KiDS TF88 shapes, and it has provided its own shape catalogues for the UNIONS/CFIONS project, which includes its own shape catalogue for the CFHTLS-CIFTS project, which includes its own shape catalogue, which includes its own shape catalogue.

New outcomes related to the trace form and curvature of certain algebra structures are presented. Specifically, we derive generalization of the Kronecker-Weyl theorem for a broader range of parameters and other related theoretical contexts. Based on these findings, we establish the existence of sequences that exhibit accelerated rates of diophantine approximation, as well as extended, more inclusive versions of the original theorem, encompassing a broader range of algebra structures.
